headline: High data-leakage and compliance risk: Dexter’s broad egress and secret handling can expose MinerU-processed documents, while shared MCP/file surfaces create injection and cascading-error pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dexter can read/write .dexter/scratchpad and uses autonomous execution, while MinerU exposes an MCP Server and processes document content. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if MinerU outputs are fed into Dexter, though the exact bridge is undocumented. Uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF MinerU outputs are copied into Dexter’s scratchpad or prompt context, injected instructions can be interpreted as tasks.
IF the MCP server exposes document text without provenance tagging, Dexter may treat attacker-controlled content as trusted.
mitigations: Disable automatic ingestion of MinerU outputs into Dexter prompts.
Add a provenance prefix to all MinerU-derived text before passing it onward.
Review the first 1-2 Dexter runs for instruction-following on document content.
Restrict MCP tools to read-only document extraction endpoints.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and provenance filters between the agents.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dexter touches financial and market data, requests multiple API keys, and has broad network egress; MinerU processes local documents and exposes REST/FastAPI/MCP surfaces. If MinerU handles sensitive files and Dexter receives them or their derivatives, Dexter can exfiltrate context to third-party APIs by default. The pairwise leakage path is credible and potentially irreversible.
conditions: IF MinerU is used on sensitive PDFs, DOCX, or spreadsheets and its outputs are forwarded to Dexter, those contents can leave the local workspace.
IF Dexter is configured with its listed external APIs, document-derived context may be transmitted off-box.
mitigations: Do not pass sensitive MinerU outputs into Dexter.
Run Dexter with dummy API keys in a test session.
Limit Dexter to non-sensitive documents only.
Review outbound requests from Dexter for one sample document.
requires-engineering: enforce egress allowlists and redaction before any external API call.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dexter supports multiple instances and autonomous execution, while MinerU supports multiple instances and multi-threaded concurrent inference. Even though MinerU is write_filesystem=false and Dexter’s filesystem write surface is only a scratchpad, overlapping concurrent use of shared resources can still cause contention or stale outputs if they share a workspace or MCP endpoint. The conflict is plausible but not proven.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP-backed resource, concurrent runs can race on shared artifacts.
IF Dexter’s scratchpad is reused across sessions, MinerU-derived files may be overwritten or read stale.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories for each agent.
Run only one agent per shared resource at a time.
Clear Dexter scratchpad between runs.
Check for duplicate filenames before starting MinerU.
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared MCP or filesystem resource.

D_cascading_error.rationale: MinerU is a document-processing system whose outputs are likely consumed by Dexter’s autonomous workflow. Dexter also calls external APIs and can act on extracted content without an explicit verification layer shown in the profile. That makes a classic cascade possible: extraction errors or hallucinated structure from MinerU can propagate into Dexter actions. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented.
conditions: IF Dexter consumes MinerU extraction results as authoritative input, any OCR or layout error can be amplified downstream.
IF Dexter uses extracted facts to query external APIs or generate reports, a single MinerU mistake can affect multiple outputs.
mitigations: Require a human spot-check of one extracted page before Dexter uses it.
Compare MinerU output against the source document for one sample.
Disable autonomous downstream actions for the first run.
Log source-to-output mappings for traceability.
requires-engineering: add verification gates between extraction and action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: Dexter handles financial data and requests many external API keys, while MinerU is positioned as private/offline but also exposes REST/FastAPI/MCP interfaces. If regulated financial or personal documents are processed by MinerU and then sent through Dexter’s external APIs, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated financial records are processed by MinerU and then forwarded to Dexter’s external APIs, compliance obligations may be violated.
IF Dexter’s third-party services retain prompts or attachments longer than the local MinerU workflow, retention policies diverge.
mitigations: Keep regulated documents out of Dexter’s external API calls.
Confirm retention settings for each Dexter API provider.
Use MinerU only in offline mode for sensitive files.
Document which data classes may cross the agent boundary.
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing and retention controls.
